meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('tasty, delicious').

examples.text: Сделай быстро вкусный кофе даме и мне.
examples.trans: Quickly make a delicious coffee for the lady and me.

examples.text: По-моему, это мясо сухое и совсем невкусное.
examples.trans: In my opinion, this meat is dry and not tasty at all.

examples.text: Сушки очень вкусные.
examples.trans: The bread rings are very tasty.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'coffee' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Сделай быстро вкусный кофе даме и мне.
examples.trans: Quickly make a delicious coffee for the lady and me.

examples.text: Я хочу кофе.
examples.trans: I want coffee.

examples.text: Кофе горячий.
examples.trans: The coffee is hot.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'lady, woman' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Сделай быстро вкусный кофе даме и мне.
examples.trans: Quickly make a delicious coffee for the lady and me.

examples.text: Деньги за зеркало я тебе потом отдам.
examples.trans: I will pay you back for the mirror later.

examples.text: То есть я отдам деньги и выйду в ноль?
examples.trans: So I give you the money and break even?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Сеня, ты чего там вдруг завис?
examples.trans: Senya, why did you freeze up over there?

examples.text: Шеф, вы не хотите мне палец сломать?
examples.trans: Chef, would you like to break my finger?

examples.text: Не будешь работать, я тебе спину сломаю!
examples.trans: If you do not work, I will break your back!

meanings.en: to put, to place, to lay down
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ложить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to put, to lay down', paired with 'класть'.

examples.text: Положи туда два сахара и свежие сливки.
examples.trans: Put two sugars and fresh cream in it.

examples.text: В гроб с собой икру не положишь!
examples.trans: You can't put caviar in your coffin to take with you!

examples.text: Положи ключи на стол.
examples.trans: Put the keys on the table.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Положи туда два сахара и свежие сливки.
examples.trans: Put two sugars and fresh cream in it.

examples.text: Прошу внести мой подарок в студию!
examples.trans: Please bring my gift into the studio!

examples.text: Тебе туда плохое мясо положили.
examples.trans: They put bad meat in there for you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'two', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Положи туда два сахара и свежие сливки.
examples.trans: Put two sugars and fresh cream in it.

examples.text: Ты мне нужен на час или два.
examples.trans: I need you for an hour or two.

examples.text: Ладно, давай двадцать тысяч, и по рукам.
examples.trans: Fine, make it twenty thousand, and we have a deal.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ахар'). Common masculine noun meaning 'sugar' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Положи туда два сахара и свежие сливки.
examples.trans: Put two sugars and fresh cream in it.

examples.text: Дай сахар, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Pass me the sugar, please.

examples.text: Я пью чай без сахара.
examples.trans: I drink tea without sugar.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'вежий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('fresh').

examples.text: Положи туда два сахара и свежие сливки.
examples.trans: Put two sugars and fresh cream in it.

examples.text: У нас как раз свежего фарша не хватает.
examples.trans: We are just short on fresh minced meat.

examples.text: Свежие ягоды на столе.
examples.trans: Fresh berries on the table.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ливки'). Common feminine noun meaning 'cream' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Положи туда два сахара и свежие сливки.
examples.trans: Put two sugars and fresh cream in it.

examples.text: Налей тёплые сливки в суп.
examples.trans: Pour warm cream into the soup.

examples.text: Вот твои сухарики, сливки и морковка.
examples.trans: Here are your croutons, cream, and carrot.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Сеня, ты чего там вдруг завис?
examples.trans: Senya, why did you freeze up over there?

examples.text: Шеф, вы не хотите мне палец сломать?
examples.trans: Chef, would you like to break my finger?

examples.text: А на следующий день он страховку оформил.
examples.trans: And the very next day he took out an insurance policy.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'шлый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('last, past').

examples.text: А в прошлом году вы что дарили?
examples.trans: And what did you give her last year?

examples.text: В прошлый раз я думала, война началась.
examples.trans: Last time I thought a war had started.

examples.text: Мы встречались на прошлой неделе.
examples.trans: We met last week.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'year' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я четыре года назад порезал себе палец.
examples.trans: Four years ago I cut my finger.

examples.text: И за четыре года нет ни одной царапины.
examples.trans: And in four years he has not had a single scratch.

examples.text: А сегодня последний день этой моей страховки.
examples.trans: And today is the very last day of this insurance of mine.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (polite/plural)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Шеф, вы не хотите мне палец сломать?
examples.trans: Chef, would you like to break my finger?

examples.text: По-моему, это просто отличный и выгодный бизнес.
examples.trans: In my opinion, it is simply great and profitable business.

examples.text: А в прошлом году вы что дарили?
examples.trans: And what did you give her last year?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to give (as a gift)', paired with 'подарить'.

examples.text: А в прошлом году вы что дарили?
examples.trans: And what did you give her last year?

examples.text: А вы сами что сегодня Кате дарите?
examples.trans: And what are you giving Katya today yourselves?

examples.text: Сеня, как думаешь, что Кате подарить?
examples.trans: Senya, what do you think I should give Katya?

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Надо срочно найти хороший подарок!
examples.trans: I must urgently find a good gift!

examples.text: Скажи быстрее, чего тебе от меня надо?
examples.trans: Tell me quickly, what do you want from me?

examples.text: Вот этот отель весь принадлежит ей!
examples.trans: This entire hotel belongs to her!

meanings.en: urgently, right away; predicative: it is urgent
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'рочно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Надо срочно найти хороший подарок!
examples.trans: I must urgently find a good gift!

examples.text: Смотрите, мы горим, всем срочно на улицу!
examples.trans: Look, we are on fire, everyone outside immediately!

examples.text: Павел Юрьевич, это срочно!
examples.trans: Pavel Yuryevich, this is urgent!

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to find', paired with 'находить'.

examples.text: Надо срочно найти хороший подарок!
examples.trans: I must urgently find a good gift!

examples.text: Где я найду грузчиков?
examples.trans: Where will I find movers?

examples.text: Я нашёл телефон.
examples.trans: I found the phone.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good').

examples.text: Надо срочно найти хороший подарок!
examples.trans: I must urgently find a good gift!

examples.text: Хорошо, проводите меня до моего номера.
examples.trans: Alright, escort me to my room.

examples.text: Хороший день.
examples.trans: A good day.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'арок'). Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'gift, present' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Надо срочно найти хороший подарок!
examples.trans: I must urgently find a good gift!

examples.text: Хотите скинуться на подарок вместе с нами?
examples.trans: Would you like to chip in for the gift with us?

examples.text: Это отличный подарок от родного отца!
examples.trans: That is an excellent gift from her own father!
